body_html:
An inspection is only as good as the time you give it, and the time of day decides how much light and how many unhurried minutes you have. A walk-around needs daylight, a counter that is not racing against closing time and a few quiet minutes before you ride away on an unfamiliar bike. A time budget for the inspection follows, then how the shop's opening hours, 09:00–21:00 daily, shape the best collection time.

How long an inspection really takes

The minutes below are a planning suggestion, not a promise about the shop. They assume you do the checks yourself and ask the staff only about the things you cannot see.

StepMinutes
Walk around the bike, photographing every side and any mark that is already there6
Test the controls: lights, indicators, horn, both brakes, throttle return5
Look at the tyres and wheels, and check the fuel gauge and odometer4
Adjust the mirrors and your seat position, and sit on the bike3
Ask how the seat lock, fuel cap and any other catch works5
Agree what is written down about condition and return5
Total28

Round it to half an hour. If you cannot give the inspection half an hour without watching the clock, the pickup time is wrong, whatever the bike looks like.

What each collection time leaves you

  • At opening, from 09:00. The whole opening day is ahead of you and the light is good. Ask whether the staff can start a handover as soon as the shop opens, instead of assuming.
  • Mid-morning to early afternoon. Daylight, no closing time in sight and room to ride a short, quiet loop before you commit to a route. This is the easiest window for a careful check.
  • Late afternoon. Still open for hours, but the light starts to fade in the cooler months and the roads are busy; the rush-hour worksheet helps you place your first ride away from the worst of it.
  • After 20:00. Closing is at 21:00. Collecting at 20:15 leaves 45 minutes, and half an hour of that is the inspection. In the dark you also cannot see a scratch, a leak or an uneven tyre.

Check the sunset time for your date before you fix the hour. In the cooler months the light can be gone well before closing time, which makes a late-afternoon collection harder than the clock suggests.

Two pickups compared

Suppose you arrive at 10:30 with no deadline. The inspection takes until about 11:00, you ride a quiet loop of ten minutes, and you leave at 11:15 with the photographs, the written note and a bike you have already ridden. Now suppose you arrive at 19:50, when it is dark in every season. The inspection runs until 20:20, and the shop closes 40 minutes later, which is little time to sort out a problem you find at the end. The bike is the same; the margin for finding and fixing a problem is not.

If you have to collect late

Sometimes a flight or a train sets the time. Then protect the inspection instead of the schedule: ask whether the handover can be done under a bright light, take the photographs with the flash on, and leave only cosmetic marks such as a scratch for the next morning's daylight check; brakes, lights, tyres and steering are checked before you ride away. Tell the shop what you could not see and ask to have it noted. If the bike is collected late in the evening, it is reasonable to ask whether the first day of the rental can begin the next morning instead; do not assume it can, since how a day is counted is for the shop to say. Keep that first ride short and slow, on roads you know.

Keep the first ride simple

Do not make the first kilometres the hardest ones. Before leaving the shop, decide where you will ride first: a quiet street where you can brake gently, check the lights at a stop and learn how the bike pulls away. If anything feels wrong, such as a spongy brake, a pull to one side or a noise you cannot place, stop somewhere safe and call the shop; if it is the brakes, walk the bike back rather than ride it.

Where to go next

The step-by-step checks themselves are in Scooter Rental Hanoi: How to Check the Bike First, and the shop's delivery and pickup guide describes how pickup works. Thuê xe máy Nguyễn Hà is at Ngõ 5 Nguyễn Văn Cừ, Bồ Đề, Long Biên, Hà Nội (near Gia Lâm bus station), phone 0334 699 969. Guides to collecting and returning a bike are gathered in the Delivery & Return Planning category.
